{{Short description|None}}
{{See also|Timeline of ancient Greek mathematicians}}
In historical times, [[Greece|Greek]] civilization has played one of the major roles in the history and development of [[Greek mathematics]]. To this day, a number of Greek mathematicians are considered for their innovations and influence on [[mathematics]].
{{Dynamic list}}
==Ancient Greek mathematicians==
This list includes mathematicians working within the Greek tradition in places outside Greece such as [[Alexandria]], Egypt, regardless of whether we know their ethnicity to be Greek.

==Modern Greek mathematicians==
*[[Leonidas Alaoglu]] (1914–1981) - Known for ''Banach- Alaoglu theorem''.<ref>{{cite book|title=Integral and Functional Analysis|first=Jie|last=Xiao|publisher=Nova Publishers|page=1996|year=2008}}</ref>
*[[Charalambos D. Aliprantis]] (1946–2009) - Founder and Editor-in-Chief of the journals Economic Theory as well as Annals of Finance.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charalambos D. Aliprantis passed away|url=https://www.springer.com/economics?SGWID=0-165-2-699309-0}}</ref> 
*[[Roger Apéry]] (1916–1994) - Professor of mathematics and mechanics at the [[University of Caen Lower Normandy|University of Caen]]. Proved the irrationality of {{math|ζ(3)}}, known as [[Apéry's constant]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Number Theory and Related Fields: In Memory of Alf van der Poorten|author1=Jonathan Borwein|author2=Igor Shparlinski|author3=Wadim Zudilin|page=5|year=2013|publisher=Springer}}</ref>
*[[Tom M. Apostol]] (1923–2016) - Professor of mathematics in [[California Institute of Technology]],<ref>{{cite book|title=The Mechanical Universe: Mechanics and Heat, Advanced Edition|author1= Richard P. Olenick|author2=Tom M. Apostol|page=588|publisher=Cambridge University Press}}</ref> he has authored a number of books about mathematics.
*[[Dimitri Bertsekas]] (1942–2026) - Member of the National Academy of Engineering professor with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. Author of fifteen books and research monographs, and coauthor of an introductory probability textbook<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edx.org/course/mitx/mitx-6-041x-introduction-probability-1296 |title=Introduction to Probability - The Science of Uncertainty |publisher=edX}}</ref>
*[[Giovanni Carandino]] (1784–1834)
*[[Constantin Carathéodory]] (1873–1950) - Mathematician who pioneered the Axiomatic Formulation of Thermodynamics.<ref>Mathematical Reviews - Volume 2003 - Page 4687, year = 2003</ref>
*[[Demetrios Christodoulou]] (born 1951) - Mathematician-physicist who has contributed in the field of general relativity.<ref>''MacArthur Fellows: The First 25 Years, 1981-2005'', p. 75- 76, John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation, 2005</ref>
*[[Constantine Dafermos]] (born 1941) - Usually notable for hyperbolic conservation laws and control theory.<ref>{{cite book|title=Semiconcave Functions, Hamilton-Jacobi Equations, and Optimal Control|author1=Piermarco Cannarsa|author2=Carlo Sinestrari|publisher=Springer|page=9}}</ref>
*[[Mihalis Dafermos]] (born 1976) - Professor of Mathematics at [[Princeton University]] and Lowndean Chair of Astronomy and Geometry at the [[University of Cambridge]]<ref>{{cite book|title=The Princeton Companion to Mathematics|author1=Timothy Gowers|author2=June Barrow-Green|author3=Imre Leader|page=17|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2010}}</ref>
*[[Apostolos Doxiadis]] (born 1953) - Australian born Mathematician.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.faber.co.uk/catalog/author/apostolos-doxiadis |title=Apostolos Doxiadis |publisher=Faber.co.uk |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140503100044/http://www.faber.co.uk/catalog/author/apostolos-doxiadis |archivedate=2014-05-03 }}</ref>
*[[Athanassios S. Fokas]] (born 1952) - Contributor in the field of integrable nonlinear partial differential equations.<ref>{{cite book|title=Algebraic Aspects of Integrable Systems: In Memory of Irene Dorfman|author1=Irene Dorfman|author2=A. S. Fokas|author3=Izrailʹ Moiseevich Gelʹfand|page=8|year=1997|publisher=Springer}}</ref>
*[[Michael Katehakis]] (born 1952) - Professor at [[Rutgers University]].<ref>{{cite book|title=New Models and Solutions for Stochastic Optimization for R&D and Transportation Problems|page=1|first=Wen|last=Chen|year=2008}}</ref>
*[[Alexander S. Kechris]] (born 1946) - Made notable contribution for the theory of Borel equivalence relations.<ref>{{cite book|title=Handbook of Set Theory|page=330|publisher=Springer|author1=Matthew Foreman|author1-link=Matthew Foreman|author2=Akihiro Kanamori|year=2009}}</ref>
*[[Nicholas Metropolis]] (1915–1999) - American born Greek physicist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scienceworld.wolfram.com/biography/Metropolis.html |title=Metropolis, Nicholas Constantine (1915-1999) - from Eric Weisstein's World of Scientific Biography |publisher=Scienceworld.wolfram.com |date=1952-03-15}}</ref>
*[[Yiannis N. Moschovakis]] (1938) - Writer, also worked as theorist in [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Descriptive Set Theory|year=1987|page=vii|first=Y.N.|last=Moschovakis}}</ref>
*[[Christos Papakyriakopoulos]] (1914–1976) - Often called ''Papa'', he specialized in [[geometric topology]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The History of Science and Technology: 1900-1970|page=704|first=Edgardo|last=Macorini|year=1988}}</ref>
*[[Athanasios Papoulis]] (1921–2002) - Contributed a number of theories, such as ''Papoulis–Gerchberg algorithm'',<ref>R. W. Gerchberg, Super-resolution through error energy reduction. Opt. Acta 21, 709-720 (1974)</ref> ''A eloquent proof'',<ref>{{cite book|title=Handbook of Fourier Analysis & Its Applications|page=223|year=2008|first=Robert J|last=Marks}}</ref> among others.
*[[Themistocles M. Rassias]] (born 1951) - Professor at the [[National Technical University of Athens]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Functional Equations, Inequalities and Applications|page=7|first=T.M.|last=Rassias|publisher=Springer|year=2003}}</ref>
*[[Raphaël Salem]] (1898–1963) - Greek mathematician after whom are named the [[Salem number]]s and whose widow founded the [[Salem Prize]].
*[[Cyparissos Stephanos]] (1857–1917) - Notable contributor of [[desmic system]]s.<ref>{{cite book|title=Applied Geometry and Discrete Mathematics: The Victor Klee Festschrift|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|author1=Peter Gritzmann|author2=Bernd Sturmfels|author3=Victor Klee|page=415}}</ref>
*[[Katia Sycara]] - Professor in the Carnegie Mellon School of Computer Science's Robotics Institute and the director of the Laboratory for Agents technology and Semantic web technologies.<ref>{{cite book|title=Terrorism Informatics: Knowledge Management and Data Mining for Homeland Security|page=39|author1=Hsinchun Chen|author2=Edna Reid|author3=Joshua Sinai|author4=Andrew Silke|author5=Boaz Ganor|year=2008|publisher=Springer|isbn=9780387716138}}</ref>
*[[Nicholas Varopoulos]] (born 1940) - Notable for his analysis on Lie groups.<ref>{{cite book |title= Random Walks and Discrete Potential Theory |page=356 |author1= M. Picardello |author2=W. Woess |date= 1999 |publisher= Cambridge University Press}}</ref>
*[[Stathis Zachos]] (born 1947) - Published a number of writings on [[computer science]].
*[[Mihail Zervos]] - Working in Department of Mathematics, [[London School of Economics]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Modern Trends in Controlled Stochastic Processes|page=161|publisher=Luniver Press|first=Alexey B.|last=Piunovskiy|year=2010|isbn=9781905986309}}</ref>
